preamble: Monophthongization of the diphthong [oi] to [uː]. In Latin, inherited *oi passed through an intermediate oe (still spelled in Republican inscriptions) and became ū in most words by the classical period: Old Latin oinos > ūnus, loidos > lūdus, coirō > cūrō. The oe spelling survived in a few words (poena beside pūnīre, moenia beside mūnīre). The change is confined to Latin; Greek oi went to [y] instead.

examples.note: From Proto-Italic *oinos, PIE *h₁óynos; cognate Old Irish óen.

examples.from: Old Latin coirō, coerō 'take care of'
